stem.en: Kabir says: "Enzymes make reactions happen that would not happen otherwise." Where is that right and where is it wrong?

text.en: Right about speed: without the enzyme, starch splits so slowly at body temperature that it never matters. Wrong about direction: the split was downhill already. The enzyme lowered the hump. It changed nothing about the valley.

feedback.en: No enzyme, a very slow reaction. The direction and the final mix are set by the Hill, not the enzyme.
They change a wait of centuries into a second. That is not nothing; it is what lets a seed run its chemistry at room temperature.
An enzyme supplies no energy. It offers a lower path. A catalyst that supplied energy would be the free-energy loop from III.6.

explanation.en: Ask what the enzyme touched. The hump, yes. The valley, never. A reaction the enzyme speeds was going to go that way anyway, given time.
